gap: No result ChatGPT got states that its top pick, the Anycubic Kobra S1, is sold on Anycubic's US store only as the $499 ACE 2 Pro Combo, and that Anycubic rates the bundled ACE 2 Pro at 48 dB with the door closed and 55 dB while drying (1 m). Both figures are above the printer's own 44 dB quiet-mode claim, and Igor's Lab measured the combo at 59.6 dB(A) while printing.
standout_why: Product Bible (cited in both chats) lists the Kobra S1 as the 'ACE 2 Pro Combo' at $499 with its ≤44/≤46 dB claims. It gives no noise figure for the ACE 2 Pro and no independent measurement of the S1. 3D Printer World (cited) prices CC2, P2S, P1S, X2D, Core One+ and Plus5 but leaves out the Kobra S1. StarterBench (cited) covers only P1S and P2S. No cited page compares price against each model's noise claim and its conditions (the CC2's ≤45 dB holds only in Silent Mode on PLA with the auxiliary fan off; the AD5M Pro's 50 dB holds only in low-noise mode). None notes that Bambu's US store pages for the P1S and P2S carry no dB claim at all.
decides: This weakens the Kobra S1 as the quietest pick. Its 44 dB is a printer-only, quiet-mode claim, but the only US listing bundles a box Anycubic itself rates at 48 to 55 dB, and the one independent figure found is 59.6 dB(A). On today's prices the Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 ($319 to $349 printer-only) is the cheapest enclosed printer with a ≤45 dB claim, though only on PLA with the auxiliary fan off. The Flashforge AD5M Pro ($379, 50 dB low-noise mode) is the next claimed figure. Our QIDI Q2 ($449) has no maker noise claim, and androidpctv measured it at 56 dB (65 dB with QIDI BOX), so it loses on noise and should not be pitched as the quiet pick.
